prediction.likelyOutcome: Lagoon should win on liability (breach) and recover the $364,212 in unpaid pre-surrender rent with high confidence. The accelerated/future-rent claim, while legally supportable given the PV-discounted liquidated-damages clause, is unlikely to be resolved on this early summary-judgment motion because of a genuine, well-supported fact dispute over mitigation and Lagoon's own redevelopment of the property — expect a partial ruling on liability/back rent now, with the future-rent amount going to further discovery and likely trial, and a probable net recovery meaningfully below the full $1,444,258 demanded for that component.

issues.label: Enforceability of Liquidated Damages / Acceleration Clause

outcome.description: The district court granted Lagoon summary judgment in June 2022, held the liquidated-damages clause enforceable so that no mitigation was required, and (after Lagoon waived attorney fees) entered judgment for $1,808,470 plus costs. The Minnesota Court of Appeals reversed on December 11, 2023, holding the liquidated-damages clause unenforceable because actual damages were capable of estimation and the clause ignored the duty to mitigate, and remanded for further proceedings on actual damages and mitigation.
outcome.finalNote: Reversed (liquidated-damages clause unenforceable) and remanded; no final figure yet.
